why: The icon-family decision (audit P1-8, backlog 10): the app declares exactly one icon package.
lucide-react is the only one already in frontend/package.json, and it ships plain SVG path data, so
react-native-svg (already a mobile dependency) can draw the same glyphs natively - no second family,
no new dependency, no hand-authored SVG. scripts/generate-icon-glyphs.mjs turns this file plus the installed
package into packages/design-system/src/icons.ts; add a name here and run `npm run icons:build`.
Some names are native-only (the More tab rows): the registry is shared, so a native-only glyph still lives here.
policies: No emoji as an icon on either platform: emoji cannot be tinted with the theme, render differently per
OEM, and are silent to screen readers. The native rows that used them now use Icon names.
No hand-authored SVG: components/MaterialIcon.tsx is frozen legacy (its importers may only be removed),
and every new glyph is a name from this registry.
Every icon import must resolve to a name in this list; __tests__/iconFamily.test.js enforces both halves.
An icon-only control still needs an accessible name; the icon itself is decorative (aria-hidden on web,
accessibilityElementsHidden on native) unless it is the only content of the control.

materialFreeze.note: components/MaterialIcon.tsx is the legacy hand-authored set (923 lines, ~220 glyphs). It is frozen: no new importer may appear, and the importer count is asserted to shrink only.
